transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-19
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Tom (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Aisha (Velvet Rail CTO), Liam (Lead ML), Nora (Platform), Ben (PM)

Auto-summary: short pilot for prototype; exploring hosted quickstart to get to first token quickly, then scope dedicated/private for production.

[00:00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're excited to learn about Velvet Rail's prototype plans. quick intro round?
[00:00:10] Aisha: yeah thanks, i'm Aisha, CTO. goal is to ship a search-rewrite and agent assist for ops, want to understand time to first token and cost tradeoffs.
[00:00:18] Liam: hi, liam here, i'll own the bench work; curious about latency - we need P95 sub 120ms for short queries if possible, also data can't leave eu for some datasets.
[00:00:27] Nora: and i'm nora on infra, we'll ask about VPC options, SSO and our KMS flows.
[00:00:31] Maya: great, i'll let Tom run the technical part, but quick note: Redwood has hosted credits for PLG quickstarts to get you to first-token under an hour usually, and we support dedicated/private for production later.
[00:00:42] Tom: thanks - couple things up front, what's the workload like? mostly short prompts or long context?
[00:00:48] Liam: mostly short, under 256 tokens, a few long doc synth jobs at night. concurrency maybe 200 rps peak in prototype.
[00:00:55] Jordan: ok that helps. for short requests we can tune batching aggressively but keep latency low; prefix caching can save tokens if you have repeated context.
[00:01:05] Ben: quick Q - is hosted going to meet our compliance? we have regs to satisfy and vendors must sign data processing addendum.
[00:01:10] Maya: yeah, hosted can be used with our standard DPA and we provide SOC2 Type II reports; for stricter needs we can move to Dedicated or Private (VPC/private control plane).
[00:01:20] Aisha: can you explain the difference in terms of latency and cost?
[00:01:24] Tom: sure. Hosted is fastest to start — we give free credits, you hit the public API endpoint, low friction. Dedicated is reserved capacity — predictable throughput and often lower per-token cost at scale because you own the GPU pool. Private (on-prem or VPC) gives you network isolation and customer-managed keys but adds some ops overhead.
[00:01:39] Liam: and how quickly can we get to first token with hosted? hours? days?
[00:01:43] Tom: in our experience, self-serve + quickstart gets devs to a successful request in less than an hour if you have basic infra; with our sample repo and Postman collection we can demo an end-to-end flow in 20-30 minutes.
[00:01:53] Nora: what about European data residency?
[00:01:56] Maya: we have EU regions; hosted lets you pick region for data residency. for additional controls we do Dedicated or Private where the control plane or data plane topology can be customer-managed.
[00:02:06] Ben: ok. what's the sizing conversation for dedicated? we might want to go dedicated in production but prototype will be hosted.
[00:02:12] Tom: sizing depends on concurrency and model choice. if you need 200 rps with a Llama2-like model quantized, you might need N GPUs; our Dedicated offering does reserved capacity and we produce throughput estimates. the quickest path: run a small bench on hosted with known model, measure CPU/GPU latency, then we propose a Dedicated config.
[00:02:28] Liam: can we run a bench with our prompts? we'd like to test real patterns not synthetic.
[00:02:32] Tom: yes, that's what we recommend. we can run a bench with your prompts; either on hosted with a controlled tenant or spin up a short dedicated bench. we'll send a small script.
[00:02:41] Aisha: on security - SSO, SAML ok? key management? audit logs?
[00:02:46] Maya: yes to all. Redwood supports SAML/SSO, fine-grained RBAC, audit logs export, KMS integrations. in Private you can use your HSM if required.
[00:02:56] Nora: any gotchas about KV cache or session reuse? we do a lot of multi-turn chat state and want to persist caches.
[00:03:03] Tom: the runtime exposes KV cache semantics and we support persistent cache pinned to session for Dedicated/Private. hosted has managed KV caching with TTLs but we can configure workarounds for prototyping. sometimes the transcripts show "K V cache" in logs — sorry transcription noise — but yes we handle it.
[00:03:17] Ben: pricing for the prototype, is it covered by credits?
[00:03:20] Maya: we'll provision PLG credits to cover the prototype usage up to an agreed amount. beyond that we can switch to pay-as-you-go.
[00:03:27] Liam: model variants — if we start with an open model and later want a smaller quantized variant, how seamless is fallback?
[00:03:33] Jordan: smooth. smart routing can fallback to a compatible model variant if capacity constrained, and compilation/kernel selection chooses the best execution path. you'll get consistent API semantics.
[00:03:43] Aisha: latency target again — can we get P95 120ms for short prompts on hosted?
[00:03:48] Tom: depends on region and model but we've seen P95 as low as 80-150ms for short prompts on hosted with optimized kernels; Dedicated gives more headroom. we'll validate in the bench.
[00:03:58] Nora: network egress — do we need special peering for VPC?
[00:04:02] Tom: for Private we can do VPC peering or on-prem package with direct connect; Dedicated has options too. we'll share our network runbook.
[00:04:10] Ben: what's the expected ops involvement if we move to Private?
[00:04:14] Maya: Private requires more infra work — installing the on-prem bundle or configuring the VPC control plane and KMS; Redwood does the initial setup with professional services if you need.
[00:04:24] Liam: any limits on token length or streaming? we need streaming for early partial outputs.
[00:04:29] Jordan: streaming is first-class; long context is supported but affects kernel selection and batching. quantify your longest context and we'll recommend model/quantization.
[00:04:38] Aisha: ok - for success criteria, we'll propose: prototype demonstrates P95 < 120ms for 90% of short queries, cost under $X/1k tokens (we'll supply target), and ability to keep specific datasets in eu. is that reasonable?
[00:04:50] Maya: absolutely. that'll be our pilot success criteria.
[00:04:54] Tom: next steps — i'll share quickstart and bench script, maya will send security docs and credits, and we should set a scoping call to size Dedicated if needed.
[00:05:02] Ben: can you also share example dashboards so our product team sees cost breakdown?
[00:05:06] Maya: yes, Redwood Console has per-route/model dashboards with token-level cost breakdowns, we'll share screenshots and a short video.
[00:05:14] Aisha: timeline — we'd like to start the prototype in one week, ship a first demo in 6 weeks.
[00:05:19] Maya: that's doable. we'll get the credits in place this week.
[00:05:23] Liam: small nit — when you send sample code, please include a minimal docker dev container so our infra folks can run it locally.
[00:05:29] Tom: will do.
[00:05:31] Jordan: also, if you want us to run an initial bench, give us ~100 example prompts and expected latencies, we can run within 48 hours once we have access.
[00:05:40] Nora: ok i'll compile those and share.
[00:05:44] Maya: perfect. any other questions?
[00:05:47] Ben: just curious about rollouts — can we do canary or A/B with model variants?
[00:05:51] Tom: yes, Redwood has rollout controls for canary, A/B, automatic fallback policies; we can set traffic splits per model version.
[00:05:59] Aisha: great, thanks everyone.
[00:06:01] Maya: thanks — we'll follow up with the pack and schedule the scoping call.

[00:06:10] (call continues with small clarifications, some cross talk, and scheduling details)

[00:21:00] Tom: quick clarification — for your doc-synthesis nightly jobs, if you want lower cost we can recommend a larger context model with quantization and batching at night to amortize cost.
[00:21:10] Liam: makes sense. also please note we have some sensitive PHI-ish logs; will need to confirm redaction and retention policies.
[00:21:17] Maya: noted — we'll include retention and redaction options in the security pack.

[00:34:30] Maya: recap and next steps: send security pack, send quickstart + bench script, schedule dedicated scoping, provision initial credits.
[00:34:40] Aisha: thanks, appreciate the speed.
[00:34:45] (meeting ends)
